title: Hermite coefficients and the Gaussian $L^2$ norm
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be the product of $n$ standard Gaussian probability measures on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belong to $L^2(\gamma_n)$. If $c_\alpha$ denotes the coefficient of $f$ against the normalized multivariate Hermite polynomial indexed by $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, then
\[\|f\|_{L^2(\gamma_n)}=\sqrt{\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}c_\alpha^2}.\]
hypotheses_covered: $f$ belongs to $L^2$ of the $n$-dimensional standard Gaussian product measure
